scope: Proposition 5.5 (Elimination with a deferred floor) of the manuscript “Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles” (preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ff8e55372a94e4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 60-61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F be a real positive scalar field on an active chart with n ordinary inputs. The following statements hold simultaneously. 1. In exact mode, along anchors where F = 0, finitely many regular changes, promotions, and exact ordinary restrictions produce a chart through those anchors on which F has identically zero formal data and hence vanishes on its real regime. All old free inputs survive. 2. If FA is visible relative to a numerical floor, there is a full-dimensional regular chart with an exact hit and F = τU, (5.10) where τ is a nonnegative-order monomial, possibly 1, and U is positive with nonzero exponent- zero value at the limiting hit. All added divisors, widths, and local conditioning costs are power moderate in |FA|. The active ordinary count does not increase. 3. If FA is negligible, active flag additions and their reference records can be chosen without realizing the floor. For every eventual realization r, field tolerance M, finite derivative request k, and record accuracy A, there is a full-dimensional regular chart hitting the input, of active ordinary count at most n, on which |F| ≤ rM . (5.11) Its added divisions and widths are power moderate in r. Its records at the hit differ from the references by O(rA), and their inverse first derivatives in the exogenous inputs, at fixed physical inputs, are O(rA) on a power-sized neighborhood. The third assertion has the following stronger order of quantifiers. For fixed M, r, k, the thickness exponents, forward bounds for the actual map and its record outputs through order at least max(k, 2), inverse-Jacobian powers, and source and physical-image neighborhood exponents can all be fixed before A is requested. Constants and sufficiently far starting points may depend on A. The denominator powers in an individual finite flattened formula may depend on A. Completed active charts remain fixed as A increases; only pending thickness recipes and their finite Taylor replays are refined. The construction also has the following prefix invariant. For the fixed request before choosing A, there is a fixed finite chronological list of coordinate replacements and scaling exponents. Every prefix has the same ordinary limiting regular equations and analytic argument germs throughout the accuracy family. Its maps and records, with the unknown of a subsequent equation still an independent ordinary input, have preassigned finite derivative and source-domain powers; its inverse and image powers are preassigned where an inverse is used. Its monomial divisors belong to powers of a fixed finite list of moderate current monomials and their triangular derivative factors. Only 60 their multiplicities inside the finite formulas can grow with accuracy. Thus the family meets the hypotheses and conclusions of Lemma 5.4 at every pending lift.
